gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is an orientation/conjugation error in the Toeplitz normal-equation matrix induced by the lag-covariance convention. ISSUE-002 concerns a different sign and vector-argument error in the generating-function quadratic-form identity and its Hermitian matrix, so it does not diagnose the normal-equation mismatch.

The gold defect is that the scalar-circulant Fourier symbols, including the frequency reversal from entrywise conjugation, were computed incorrectly, yielding incorrect actual 2-by-2 Fourier blocks. ISSUE-004 identifies a separate invalid swap-matrix similarity used to prove spectral symmetry; its corrected diagonal similarity does not diagnose the scalar-circulant symbol computation or the resulting block formula.

The gold defect is the unestablished reality of quaternion PCG recurrence parameters and the resulting real-coefficient polynomial representation. ISSUE-005 instead concerns an inequality-direction error when extending a product bound and the repair of its constant, with no diagnosis of PCG scalar-parameter reality or coefficient commutation.
